items.claim: The single witness records a closed-section mark on MT 4:3 — the verse that ends the tile act with the sign declaration א֥וֹת הִ֖יא לְבֵ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל — and a second one on MT 4:15; the row names only MT 4:12 and MT 4:14 among the closed-section marks inside 4:1-4:17, and it refuses the 4:3/4:4 division from the onset side alone. The mark on MT 4:3 falls exactly on the division the row rejects.
items.both_sides: Behind the 4:3/4:4 seam: MT 4:3 ends on the sign declaration to the house of Israel and the witness marks a closed section there. Ahead of it: MT 4:4 opens וְאַתָּ֤ה שְׁכַב֙, the bare pronoun with a fresh lying command, without the 'and you, son of man' address that stands at 4:1 and at 5:1 — but MT 4:3 itself opens וְאַתָּ֤ה קַח לְךָ֙, the same bare pronoun with the same 'take for yourself' imperative, so the onset test the row applies does not separate 4:3 from 4:4 either. Carrying the span forward: the ropes at 4:8 and one rationing arc to 4:17, whose open-section mark the row does cite. A closed-section mark informs and never decides, so the span can stand; it cannot stand on the stated ground, which weighs only what 4:4 lacks.

suggested_fix.fact: a closed-section mark on MT 4:3, whose final clause is the sign declaration, and a second closed-section mark on MT 4:15

items.claim: The row's stated ground — that none of the section marks inside 5:1-5:17 coincides with a formula onset — is false on the witness at four seams: the open-section mark on MT 5:4 stands before the messenger formula the row itself cites at 5:5 (כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֔ה); the closed-section marks on MT 5:6 and MT 5:7 stand before the two 'therefore' messenger formulas at 5:7 (לָכֵ֞ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה, addressing a plural) and at 5:8 (לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה הִנְנִ֥י עָלַ֖יִךְ, addressing a feminine singular); and the open-section mark on MT 5:10 stands before the oath and the utterance signature at 5:11. Separately, MT 5:13 reads וְֽיָדְע֞וּ כִּי אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֗ה דִּבַּ֨רְתִּי֙ — the third-person recognition refrain governing 'I Yahweh have spoken' — so the verse the row rejects as unit-final carries a stacked close, and its recognition member is nowhere disclosed.
items.both_sides: At 5:4/5:5: behind, the burning and scattering of the hair ends and the witness marks an open section; ahead, the messenger formula opens the interpretation — so a mark and a formula onset do meet there. At 5:7/5:8: behind, a plural address; ahead, a feminine singular address after a closed-section mark, which is a person-and-number shift rather than an absence of coincidence. At 5:13/5:14: behind, a stacked close, recognition refrain plus 'I Yahweh have spoken'; ahead, MT 5:14 opens וְאֶתְּנֵךְ֙ לְחָרְבָּ֣ה with no onset device at all, and no section mark stands at 5:13. That pairing is what actually holds the span together, along with the clause closing both 5:2 and 5:12, וְחֶ֖רֶב אָרִ֥יק אַחֲרֵיהֶֽם, word-for-word and verse-final in each. The span keeps its extent; the ground given for it does not survive.

suggested_fix.fact: the open-section mark on MT 5:4 falls at the seam where 5:5's messenger formula opens the interpretation, and MT 5:13 carries the third-person recognition refrain governing 'I Yahweh have spoken'

items.claim: Two devices inside 6:1-6:10 go undisclosed by role: MT 6:3 carries a messenger formula (כֹּה אָמַ֣ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְ֠הוִה), and MT 6:2 carries the 'son of man' address next to the set-your-face command (בֶּן אָדָ֕ם שִׂ֥ים פָּנֶ֖יךָ). Every Hebrew fact the row does state is true on the bytes, including the strict word-event at 6:1, the recognition members at 6:7 and 6:10, the K/Q at 6:3, and the 28-verse count for the third-person refrain.
items.both_sides: At 6:10/6:11: behind, the third-person recognition refrain with an open-section mark on that verse; ahead, a fresh messenger formula with a change of addressee. The undisclosed formula at 6:3 does not move that seam, since it stands inside the oracle it opens, but it is the same device class that carries the onset case at 6:11, so a reader weighing that seam needs to see that a messenger formula inside 6:1-6:10 did not cut.

suggested_fix.fact: a messenger formula at MT 6:3 and the 'son of man' address at MT 6:2, disclosed by role

items.claim: The span carries two devices the row never names: an open-section mark on MT 6:14, the unit's own closing verse, and a second-person recognition member at MT 6:13 (וִֽידַעְתֶּם֙ כִּֽי אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֔ה), which is refrain-grade close evidence standing one verse before the close the row does cite at 6:14 (וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה). The row's statement that both edges of the unit are marked is true, but the mark at the closing edge is never sourced.
items.both_sides: At 6:10/6:11: behind, the third-person recognition refrain at 6:10 with an open-section mark on that verse; ahead, the messenger formula at 6:11 turning from the mountains to a gesture command for the prophet. At 6:13/6:14: behind, a refrain-grade recognition member; ahead, 6:14 opens on a stretched-out-hand clause with no onset device, so no cut arises there — but that is a judgment the row has to state, since a refrain of that family closes the unit before it elsewhere in this same stretch.

items.claim: MT 7:2 carries the 'and you, son of man' sub-onset together with a messenger formula in one clause (וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן אָדָ֗ם כֹּה אָמַ֞ר אֲדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה), inside a four-verse span, and the row discloses neither device, although it does disclose the K/Q at that same verse. That sub-onset is the device opening the two sign-act units at 4:1 and 5:1, so its role here — corroboration following the word-event rather than a competing onset — is exactly what a four-verse row needs to state.
items.both_sides: At 7:1: behind, the recognition close at 6:14 with an open-section mark on that verse; ahead, the word-event in its strict form, identical byte-for-byte with the one at 6:1 and with the one inside 3:16, standing on 39 verses book-wide. At 7:4/7:5: behind, the second-person recognition member with an open-section mark on 7:4; ahead, a fresh messenger formula. Both edges hold; only the in-span disclosure is short.

suggested_fix.fact: the 'and you, son of man' sub-onset and the messenger formula both standing at MT 7:2

items.claim: At 7:5 the English the row attaches to its splice covers the whole verse — the messenger clause and then 'a disaster, a unique disaster, behold, it comes' — while the Hebrew spliced at that ref is only the four-word messenger clause (כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה). The announcement the extra English renders stands in MT 7:5 beyond the splice (רָעָ֛ה אַחַ֥ת רָעָ֖ה הִנֵּ֥ה בָאָֽה) and is never quoted, so the gloss reaches past what it glosses.
items.both_sides: At 7:4/7:5: behind, the second-person recognition member with an open-section mark on 7:4; ahead, the messenger formula. At 7:9/7:10: behind, the recognition member with its appended participle (וִֽידַעְתֶּ֕ם כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה מַכֶּֽה) carrying the eye-and-pity refrain it shares with 7:4, 5 verses book-wide at MT 5:11, 7:4, 7:9, 8:18 and 9:10, re-derived here and matching the row; ahead, 7:10 opens with no onset device. No section mark stands at 7:9 and the row states that absence correctly. The boundary is sound; the defect is the reach of the English.

items.claim: The open-section mark the row discloses on MT 7:22 falls at the very seam the row rejects as translation-layer paragraphing, and MT 7:23 turns from the third-person doom description to an imperative addressed to the prophet (עֲשֵׂ֖ה הָֽרַתּ֑וֹק). The rejection is argued against the English paragraph breaks alone and never weighs the Masoretic section standing at the same place, while the mark itself is disclosed elsewhere in the row as texture.
items.both_sides: At 7:22/7:23: behind, MT 7:22 ends on the profaning of the hidden place and the single witness marks an open section there; ahead, MT 7:23 opens on an imperative to the prophet, and the English paragraphing agrees — but that agreement is translation-layer and carries nothing. Against the cut: an imperative is not one of the onset devices that open a row in this book, since no word-event, no messenger formula and no set-your-face stands at 7:23, and the unit's recognition close does not arrive until 7:27 (וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה), which carries its own open-section mark. The span holds at low confidence; the ground has to be the missing onset device and not the tier of the English break.

suggested_fix.fact: an open-section mark on MT 7:22 standing at the same seam as the imperative onset at MT 7:23

unresolved_uncertainty.what: No row in this cluster carries a dated-block disclosure, and the row shape itself has no field for one.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: If that disclosure is required, the gap is corpus-wide rather than particular to these seven rows and should be decided once, not repaired row by row.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: Whether a closed-section mark standing exactly on a seam a row explicitly rejects raises the duty above disclosure-as-corroboration — the case at MT 4:3, where the mark falls on the rejected division and that verse also ends on a sign declaration.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: It decides whether 4:1-4:17 needs only an added disclosure or a re-argued rejection, and the same question returns at MT 7:22/7:23.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: The inventory does not record where inside a verse a section mark falls, so I could not test whether any mark in this span sits inside its verse rather than after it.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: Every mark finding above is therefore stated at the verse level, and none of them asserts a place inside a verse.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: Whether the two short units at 7:5-7:9 and 7:10-7:27 are the right shape for the 'end' oracle at all: the Masoretic sectioning of this chapter runs 7:1-4, 7:5-22, 7:23-27, which agrees with the row division at 7:4/7:5 and with nothing else in it.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: The 7:9/7:10 seam rests on a recognition member alone and the 7:10-7:27 row runs 18 verses, past the stretch cap; the division agreeing with the witness would be 7:5-7:22 and 7:23-7:27, which no row in this cluster proposes.

e19_selfreport: I ran no listing, no glob, no wildcard and no recursive search at any point — not against SP, not against the worktree, and not against my own scratch. Every file I opened was named in my brief, in my launch message, in my own global policy, or in the authority note, and each was opened by its exact path. My private working files went into a uniquely named subdirectory of this session's own scratchpad, and the deliverable was written straight to the path my launch message named, with no existence check of any directory.
